traits.leaf_incision.note: DELTA, Convolvulaceae (read 2026-10-17): undivided blades, sometimes lobed; some dissected, pinnatifid or palmatifid. FOC: lobing in one Dinetus species and Hewittia.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Flora of China Convolvulaceae (read 2026-10-17): margins entire in Dichondra, Dinetus, Erycibe, entire or 3-lobed in Hewittia; DELTA gives no toothed state.

traits.flowering_position.note: Wikipedia Ipomoea (read 2026-10-16) (largest genus): flowers axillary, solitary or in cymes; APweb Solanales page: Humbertia flowers single and axillary. Would otherwise inherit terminal.

traits.carpels.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 428: ovary of 2, rarely 3 to 5, carpels.

traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 428, 505: Simpson calls the flowers hypogynous. Simpson p. 505 defines hypogynous and epigynous as flowers without a hypanthium.

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 322 Convolvulaceae (order Solanales): herbaceous or woody, often climbing, the sap usually milky; leaves alternate, simple; no stipules; flowers regular, bisexual; sepals usually free; corolla united, 5-lobed, pleated in bud; stamens 5, low on the corolla tube; ovary of 1 to 4 cells, superior (the order's); fruit a capsule, or fleshy and staying shut. The funnel-shaped corolla of the bindweeds and morning glories is from common knowledge, inferred, not traced.

traits.rosette.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Convolvulaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Cuscutaceae, Humbertiaceae: whether the leaves gather in rosettes (character 22), coded no rosette. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 427, 428, family Convolvulaceae: phyllotaxis pattern spiral, usually; read as {"spiral": "usually"}.

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 427, 428, family Convolvulaceae: inflorescence head, dichasium or solitary flowers, usually; read as {"cyme": "often", "head": "often", "solitary": "often"}.

traits.sexual_system.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 427, 428, family Convolvulaceae: sexual system hermaphrodite; read as "hermaphrodite".

traits.fruit_type.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add drupe (sometimes), nut (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 427, 428: capsule, berry, drupe or nut.
